name: AIPAC

summary.text: The American Israel Public Affairs Committee (AIPAC) is a U.S. lobbying organization founded in 1959 that works to shape U.S. policy toward Israel. For most of its history it did not fund candidates directly; in December 2021 it created a traditional PAC (AIPAC PAC) and in January 2022 a super PAC, United Democracy Project (UDP), which can spend unlimited sums on independent expenditures. In the 2024 cycle UDP spent more than $14 million in the Democratic primary that unseated Rep. Jamaal Bowman (NY-16) and more than $8 million in the primary that unseated Rep. Cori Bush (MO-1), according to federal filings as reported by FactCheck.org, NPR and the Associated Press.

facts.claim: AIPAC describes itself on its website as a grassroots organization whose mission is to persuade the U.S. government to adopt policies that build a durable, mutually beneficial relationship with Israel; it says it is funded by Americans, is not directed or funded by the Israeli government, supports pro-Israel candidates in both parties and opposes anti-Israel candidates in both parties, and identifies United Democracy Project as an AIPAC-backed super PAC.
facts.quote: leading the political fight to keep Congress pro-Israel

sources.title: About AIPAC
Politics

facts.claim: AIPAC, established in 1959, historically did not contribute to individual candidates' campaigns. It announced plans for a PAC and a super PAC in December 2021; AIPAC PAC was created on December 15, 2021 and United Democracy Project, its super PAC, was established on January 3, 2022. AIPAC PAC may give at most $5,000 per election to a candidate, while UDP cannot give to candidates but may raise and spend unlimited amounts advocating for or against federal candidates.
facts.quote: AIPAC PAC, which was created Dec. 15, 2021, and that United Democracy Project, AIPAC's super PAC, was established on Jan. 3, 2022

sources.title: United Democracy Project

facts.claim: In the June 25, 2024 Democratic primary in New York's 16th district, United Democracy Project spent almost $9.9 million opposing Rep. Jamaal Bowman and nearly $4.8 million supporting George Latimer, according to FactCheck.org's review of FEC data; press reports put the total at about $14.5 million to $14.7 million, the most ever spent by one group on a House primary. Latimer won with over 58% of the vote to about 41% for Bowman.
facts.quote: almost $9.9 million to oppose Bowman and nearly $4.8 million to support Latimer

sources.title: United Democracy Project

facts.claim: Many of the United Democracy Project television ads in the Bowman race made scant mention of Israel and instead focused on infrastructure spending and local issues, including a claim that Bowman voted against replacing lead pipes; Newsweek, citing AdImpact, reported that many of the group's ads did not focus on Israel. One May 2024 UDP ad featured Elisha Wiesel, son of Elie Wiesel, asking voters to back Latimer.
facts.quote: many of the TV ads attacking Bowman or praising Latimer made scant mention of Israel, and instead focused on infrastructure spending and other issues of local concern

facts.claim: Bowman said in an interview that none of the ads against him talked about Israel, and that they instead argued he was not a real Democrat over his vote on part of a Biden-supported bill.
facts.quote: Zero per cent [of the ads] talked about Israel

sources.title: AIPAC, the US pro-Israel lobby, spends big but faces backlash ahead of midterm elections

facts.claim: After Latimer's win, AIPAC posted on X on June 26, 2024 that the result was 'a major victory for the Democratic mainstream that stands with the Jewish state and a defeat for the extremist fringe,' and told NBC New York that the outcome showed the pro-Israel position is 'both good policy and good politics' for both parties.
facts.quote: This triumph by a strong pro-Israel candidate represents a major victory for the Democratic mainstream that stands with the Jewish state and a defeat for the extremist fringe.

sources.title: Latimer defeats Bowman in Democratic primary
Israel Critic Jamaal Bowman Loses Most Expensive House Primary Ever

facts.claim: In the August 6, 2024 Democratic primary in Missouri's 1st district, United Democracy Project spent more than $8.4 million against Rep. Cori Bush, far more than any other outside group, according to federal campaign finance records reported by the Associated Press; Bush lost to St. Louis County prosecutor Wesley Bell in the state's most expensive nominating contest on record.
facts.quote: spent more than $8.4 million against Bush in the Aug. 6 Democratic primary, according to federal campaign finance records

sources.title: A pro-Israel super PAC helped defeat one Squad member. Now it's going after another, Cori Bush

facts.claim: AIPAC told the Associated Press that its grassroots members back pro-Israel progressive Democrats like Wesley Bell, and described Cori Bush as one of the most hostile critics of Israel in Congress.
facts.quote: its grassroots members back pro-Israel progressive Democrats like Wesley Bell

sources.title: A pro-Israel super PAC helped defeat one Squad member. Now it's going after another, Cori Bush

facts.claim: As of September 22, 2024, United Democracy Project had spent about $56 million in the 2024 cycle, of which more than $35.6 million was independent expenditures, according to OpenSecrets data cited by FactCheck.org; OpenSecrets' August 2024 analysis said most of UDP's congressional spending went to efforts to oust Democratic incumbents over their criticism of Israel's military response to the October 7 Hamas attack.
facts.quote: United Democracy Project also has spent about $56 million, and, as of Sept. 22, more than $35.6 million of it was on independent expenditures

sources.title: United Democracy Project

facts.claim: UDP's largest donors include WhatsApp co-founder Jan Koum, Home Depot co-founder Bernie Marcus, hedge-fund founder Paul Singer and New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft, according to FactCheck.org.
facts.quote: Among UDP's largest donors are WhatsApp co-founder Jan Koum, Home Depot co-founder Bernie Marcus, hedge-fund founder Paul Singer, and New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft.

connections.claim: AIPAC established United Democracy Project, a super PAC, on January 3, 2022; AIPAC's website identifies it as an AIPAC-backed super PAC that works to defeat candidates it considers detractors of the U.S.-Israel relationship.
connections.quote: United Democracy Project, AIPAC's super PAC, was established on Jan. 3, 2022
